d.techtimes.com/en/full/471742/naomi-bas.note: The outlet's photograph of the person the story is about, at a chess tournament. Not a picture of a BCI, but it is this press item's own picture of its subject, which is what the rule asks for.

mma.prnewswire.com/media/3005813/newroni.note: The Newronika wordmark on white. A logo is a mark, not a picture, and says nothing about the CE mark the release announces.

ovid.com//images/og_image_white.webp.note: The Wolters Kluwer corporate logo, served as Ovid's default og:image. The platform's mark, not the paper's.

arxiv.org/static/browse/0.3.4/images/arx.note: The arXiv logo, served as the og:image on every abs page. Nothing to do with any individual preprint.

d2csxpduxe849s.cloudfront.net/media/e326.note: A posed stock photograph of an EEG session, used as Frontiers in Neurology masthead art. A real photograph, but it was queued for a paper on octopolar DBS electrodes in surgery and shows none of that. This is the case the depicts field was added for.

arxiv.org/html/2608.02083v1/fig1.png.note: The paper's own Figure 1: an EEG electrode montage schematic with a nine-entry colour legend. gray-knoe-prod.gtv-cdn.com/resizer/v2/r5.note: A KNOE 8 broadcast frame-grab. Publishing it would reproduce another broadcaster's branding and a third party's advert.

spectrum.ieee.org/media-library/three-hi.note: IEEE Spectrum's photograph of the scholarship winners named in the story. A step-and-repeat group shot, which is weak but is genuinely of the story.
